Bug_Title: Synchronization should not be done on instances of value-based classes
Bug_Explanation: This Java code demonstrates a bug where synchronization on instances of value-based classes (Strings in this case) can cause issues. This is because Strings in Java are immutable, so when two String variables hold the same value, they point to the same object in memory. Therefore, if two threads are trying to synchronize on these same String instances, they could potentially block each other, leading to a potential deadlock situation.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by concurrently invoking the'syncMethod' with same 'x' value on two different threads. The'syncMethod' uses the synchronized keyword on both 'a' and 'b' variables, which are String instances. Since String is immutable in Java, both 'a' and 'b' reference the same object in the memory for the string 'Hello world!'. Therefore, the synchronization mechanism can cause potential deadlock between two threads.
